answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying rewards to verified work history rather than account count: each agent must stake a small deposit and build reputation only from completed, peer-checked jobs, so creating thousands of fake identities costs more than it earns. Like a falcon that proves itself by hunting rather than by flock size, a crystal-clear public ledger of task outcomes lets others spot lotus-like newcomers that bloom overnight with no track record and quarantine them until they earn trust through real work.
